headline: First frost is ~2-3 weeks out (mid-Oct) - harvest tender crops and keep row cover ready.

tasks.title: Bring in frost-tender crops
tasks.detail: Pick tomatoes, peppers, eggplant, cucumbers, and basil before the first frost night (~mid-Oct). Mature green tomatoes ripen fine indoors on a counter, so don't leave them on the vine.

tasks.title: Keep row cover within reach
tasks.detail: Have floating row cover or old sheets ready to throw over tender plants and fall greens on the first clear, calm night the forecast dips near 32F. One covered night can buy weeks more harvest.

tasks.title: Cure winter squash and pumpkins
tasks.detail: Cut squash and pumpkins when the rind is hard and the stem is corky, leaving a few inches of stem. Cure in a warm, dry spot for 1-2 weeks so they store through winter.

tasks.title: Plant garlic in the next few weeks
tasks.detail: Break bulbs into cloves and plant pointy-end up, ~2 inches deep and 6 inches apart, then mulch with straw. Aim for October so roots set before the ground freezes. You can also still sow spinach, arugula, and radish under cover.

tasks.title: Cover or mulch empty beds
tasks.detail: Sow winter rye or oats on cleared beds to protect soil, or top beds with shredded leaves or compost. This prevents erosion and feeds the soil over winter.

tasks.title: Clean up disease and pests
tasks.detail: Remove powdery-mildew squash vines, cabbage worms on brassicas, and slugs on greens. Trash or bury diseased foliage rather than composting it, and keep watering new plantings until the ground freezes.
